critical_steps: Four copies of H with weights 1/2 form a Parseval fusion frame.
Replacing every copy by span{e2} satisfies the theorem's per-index perturbation bound with epsilon 1/2.
The perturbed energy vanishes on e1, contradicting the claimed positive lower bound 3/4.
A global square-sum perturbation estimate gives the exact repaired lower bound A-epsilon^2 and upper bound B.
For N finite indices, the per-index theorem hypothesis can only yield A-N epsilon^2 in general, and repeated-subspace examples make the factor N sharp.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact four-block counterexample in R^2 and an exact energy-difference identity.
integrity.unproved_limits: No complete classification of perturbation metrics for nonordered controlled subspaces is claimed.

limitations: The finding refutes Theorem 4.9 and supplies a global square-sum repair.
The sharp N-factor statement is for finite index sets under the theorem's literal pointwise hypothesis.
The repair uses the positivity implicit in the source's square-root expression; other perturbation metrics can require different constants.

title: Pointwise fusion-subspace perturbations do not aggregate into a frame bound
